A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spectron study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original FineWeb pretraining results, downstream evaluations, ablations, spectral diagnostics and 39-run scaling-law experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds rank comparisons, runtime measurements, additional method comparisons and spectral diagnostics.

M1.justification: The core Spectron update and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. Appendix G adds a CoLA+Spectron variant with nonlinear factorization and compositions with ReLoRA and SST, extending the method beyond the original linear-factor training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb pretraining and HellaSwag, PIQA and ARC Easy evaluation. The added studies vary ranks, architectures, optimizers and timing measurements without introducing new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds evaluated comparisons with LoRO, CoLA, ReLoRA and SST, including their Spectron combinations. Appendix B.2 also adds AdamW, self-guided and dense comparators to the rank study. These substantially broaden the comparison set beyond v1's retained baselines.

E3.justification: Additional evaluations introduce rank ratio 0.5, wall-clock time as a metric, and comparator configurations distinguished by architecture changes, warm starts and auxiliary parameters. The original validation split, training budgets, batch size, sequence length and model configurations remain unchanged; model renaming does not establish a setting change.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary validation: Table 4 and Figure 13 test optimizer performance across ranks, Appendix F examines practical runtime overhead, Appendix G tests compatibility with other training approaches, and Figure 15 adds layer-7 attention and feedforward spectral diagnostics. The original component, learning-rate and FFN-only ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The 39 scaling experiments and their fitting procedures are retained; additional result entries do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1, the original ablation results and scaling fits are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 4 and 7–9 and Figure 15. New comparisons include CoLA perplexity 24.21 versus 19.95 with Spectron, ReLoRA 26.06 versus 22.70 with Spectron, and SST 29.40 versus 23.40 with Spectron, alongside runtime measurements. These are additional comparisons, not improvements to retained same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds Equations 25–26, using a bounded ReLU activation mask to argue that the linear spectral perturbation bound extends to nonlinear factorization. The original spectral derivation and scaling-law mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the central claims: stable native low-rank pretraining without auxiliary dense weights, competitive performance at equal FLOPs, and compute-optimal scaling with inference benefits. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that frontier-scale validation remains open and that its implementation trains more slowly than dense models. It attributes the runtime gap to unfused matrix multiplications and data-loading overhead, and interprets the new hybrid results as evidence of complementarity. The original instability and scaling interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and specifies two nodes with four H100 GPUs each connected by InfiniBand for the timing analysis. It also reports training times and implementation bottlenecks. Existing Appendix E hyperparameters and training details are retained; the repository's contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning against closely related approaches through LoRO, CoLA, ReLoRA and SST, distinguishing architectural changes, auxiliary full-rank storage and optimizer-level compatibility. Section 2 also adds structured-layer scaling, Bayesian low-rank work and further gradient-orthogonalization references.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. Changes include renaming Transformer-S/M/L to parameter-specific Llama names, adding limitations and impact statements, updating publication information, and inserting new appendix sections before the retained training curves. There is no extensive rewrite of the main narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables covering rank comparisons, runtime, recent methods and warm-start/parameter distinctions, plus a rank-comparison plot and a 15-panel spectral diagnostic figure. Existing graphical content is retained, with some relocation and renumbering: v1 Figures 13 and 14 become v2 Figures 14 and 16. The additions substantially expand the visual presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons, runtime measurements and explicit limitations improve empirical breadth and transparency beyond v1's largely FLOP-based efficiency assessment. Reporting slower dense-relative runtime is particularly useful. The net gain is qualified by briefly documented settings for the new comparisons and Appendix G.1's nonlinear guarantee, whose derivation does not address changes in the data-dependent ReLU mask. The established main results remain intact.
